meta.title: SAT Dojo · a gym for SAT solvers · Hashi
meta.description: Submit your SAT solver as WebAssembly and climb the leaderboard: scored on hidden, fresh formulas with deterministic fuel, not seconds. Free, open source.

title: SAT Dojo
intro: A gym for SAT solvers. Compile yours to WebAssembly, submit it, and it is scored on a hidden set of fresh formulas: Hashi puzzles, parity traps, random 3-SAT, pigeons, queens, factoring, multiplier miters, graph coloring and one mystery family.

seasons.meta_description: Every finished season of the SAT Dojo: the final leaderboard, the revealed seed, the hidden set and every result per formula, ready to download and check.
seasons.title: Season archive
seasons.intro: When a season ends, its leaderboard is frozen and everything is published: the seed of the hidden set, the set itself and the result of every solver on every formula.
seasons.versions: Generator v{{ generator }} · rules v{{ rules }}
seasons.sealed: The seed stays secret until the season ends, then it is revealed here.
seasons.no_set: No set was archived for this season; regenerate it from the seed.
seasons.empty_board: No solver was ranked this season.
seasons.none: No season has ended yet. The archive starts when season {{ season }} is over.
seasons.verify: The SHA-256 of the revealed seed has to match the commitment published at the start. With the same generator version, dojo export regenerates the set from the seed; the archived set stays valid for good, and dojo run --set scores any solver on it exactly like the leaderboard did.

how.title: How it works
how.build: Any language that compiles to WASI preview 1 works: Rust, C and C++ with wasi-sdk, Zig, Go. Read DIMACS on stdin and answer like in the SAT competition.
how.proof: UNSAT needs a proof, like in the SAT Competition: your program gets a file path as its first argument and writes a DRAT proof there (text or binary), or LRAT after printing c proof lrat. Without a proof the answer counts as unsolved, a wrong proof disqualifies.
how.train: Score your solver locally on the public dev set with the dojo tool. It runs exactly like the leaderboard, so you know your score before you submit.
how.submit: Upload the .wasm file. It runs on the hidden set of the current season, on our own machine.
how.climb: The lowest PAR-2 wins: the mean fuel per formula, where unsolved formulas count twice the budget.

family.title: The formulas
family.hashi_text: Hashiwokakero puzzles from 12×12 to 28×28 as CNF, without the connectivity rule. Always satisfiable.
family.hashi_parity_text: Puzzles with one number changed so the numbers add up to an odd sum. Unsatisfiable, since every bridge adds two. Easy to see, hard to prove by resolution.
family.random_3sat_text: Uniform random 3-SAT at the phase transition, 4.26 clauses per variable, about half of them satisfiable.
family.pigeonhole_text: n+1 pigeons in n holes: the classic that needs exponentially long resolution proofs. Plus a few that do fit.
family.queens_text: N queens on boards up to 64×64 with a few forbidden squares.
family.factoring_text: A multiplier circuit with its output fixed to a number of 16 to 26 bits: satisfiable when it is the product of two primes, unsatisfiable when it is a prime. Cryptography in miniature.
family.miter_text: Two multipliers wired differently, asked for an input on which they disagree: unsatisfiable when both are correct, satisfiable when one hides a rarely triggered bug. Hardware verification in miniature.
family.coloring_text: Four colors for random graphs near the threshold: some with a planted coloring, some containing a Mycielski graph that needs five.
family.tseitin_text: Parity constraints on the edges of a random regular graph, unsatisfiable when the charges add up to an odd number. Exponentially hard for resolution.
family.quasigroup_text: Latin squares with 42% of their cells emptied, to be completed. Always satisfiable, and hardest around that share of holes.
family.hamiltonian_text: A cycle through every vertex of a bipartite graph: planted, or impossible because the two sides differ in size.
family.mystery_text: Every hidden set has one more family that the dev set doesn't have, drawn from a reserve by the season's seed. It counts like the others, shows up as the mystery family and is revealed in the archive when the season ends.
family.community_text: Benchmarks from the community pool: a few in every hidden set, drawn by the season's seed and published with their authors when the season ends.

fair.title: Fair play
fair.fuel: Fuel counts the WebAssembly operators a solver executes, weighted the way a real processor pays for them: loads and stores three units, locals and constants nothing, everything else one, bulk memory one per byte. Clocks and random numbers are seeded, so a solver gets the same score on every machine, every time.
fair.calibrated: Counting instructions is criticised because a memory access can cost far more than an addition. So we measured: seven solvers, MiniSat, CaDiCaL and Kissat among them, on 180 formulas, natively and in the sandbox. Within every solver, fuel follows native time with a rank correlation of 0.91 to 1.00, and it ranks the solvers almost exactly like their running time. Weighting memory and making locals free predicts time across solvers about a tenth better than one unit per operator. Method, data and limits: CALIBRATION.md.
fair.hidden: The test set comes from a secret seed that changes every season, and every formula is scrambled: variables renamed and negated, clauses shuffled. While a season runs, results are shown per family only, never per formula.
fair.heldout: In 2026 an AI-generated solver with more than a hundred family-specific sub-solvers beat every main-track solver on the satisfiable instances of the SAT Competition, and the organizers called memorization versus generalization an open problem. So the hidden set goes beyond the dev set: larger formulas, and one family your solver has never trained on.
fair.checked: Models are verified against the formula, and every UNSAT answer needs a proof, checked like in the main track of the SAT Competition: drat-trim turns it into LRAT and cake_lpr, a checker proven correct in HOL4 and compiled by CakeML, has the last word. Our own labels are proven the same way. A wrong model or a rejected proof disqualifies the submission, so guessing never pays.
fair.sandbox: No network, no environment, and no files but the one for the proof. Memory, output and the proof are capped, and submissions run on a separate machine that holds no data.
fair.accounts: Accounts have to be a day old to submit, and there are three submissions a day per account and per network. Identical code is refused, even renamed or padded, and only your best submission is ranked.
fair.seasons: A new season brings a new hidden set and every submission is evaluated again. The finished season is archived: its final leaderboard, its set and every result per formula are published.
fair.copies: Scores are exact, so a solver leaves a fingerprint: the fuel it uses on every formula. A submission that behaves like an earlier one by someone else isn't ranked. Changing a copy enough to escape that makes it a different solver, and making it slower only puts it below the original.
fair.commit: At the start of a season we publish the SHA-256 of its secret seed. When the season is over the seed is revealed, so anyone can check that the set was fixed beforehand and regenerate it with dojo export --seed.

science.title: For researchers
science.text: Fuel is deterministic, so results are reproducible and comparable between papers: name the season and the dev seed. The leaderboard is available as JSON at /dojo/board.json, the harness is open source.

industrial.title: Industrial track
industrial.intro: Real instances from past SAT Competition main tracks: hardware verification and bounded model checking, cryptography, scheduling, planning and software verification, fetched from the Global Benchmark Database.
industrial.budget: About 200 times the Sprint budget per formula, and up to 4 GB of memory per run.
industrial.proofs: Every UNSAT answer needs a proof, checked as in the Sprint.
industrial.why: With half a second per formula, MiniSat beats CaDiCaL and Kissat: their inprocessing only pays off on large industrial instances. Given minutes, the big solvers can show what they do, closer to the SAT Competition.
industrial.fee: Entry will cost a small fee that covers the compute.
industrial.board_note: The Industrial track is coming soon: real SAT Competition instances, minutes per formula.

community.meta_title: Bring your own benchmark · SAT Dojo
community.meta_description: Submit a CNF formula to the SAT Dojo's community pool. Verified, hard instances join the hidden sets of later seasons and are published with your name.
community.title: Bring your own benchmark
community.intro: Like the SAT Competition, the Dojo takes benchmarks from its participants. Submit a formula you care about: if its answer can be settled for certain, it isn't too easy and a moderator accepts it, it joins the pool. Every season's hidden set draws a few from the pool, and they are published with your name when the season ends.
community.rule_answer: A certain answer: within a minute, splr finds a model we check, or proves the formula unsatisfiable with a proof the verified checker accepts.
community.rule_easy: Not too easy, like in the SAT Competition: MiniSat must not solve it with a tenth of the fuel a solver gets per formula.
community.rule_size: At most 2 MB of DIMACS, 200,000 variables and a million clauses. Duplicates are refused, also renamed or shuffled ones.
community.rule_draw: Each season draws up to {{ count }}: at most two per author and two per family, rare authors and families first, as many SAT as UNSAT. The draw is seeded with the season's secret seed and fixed when the season starts.
community.rule_license: You license the formula under CC BY 4.0, so it can be published with the season's set.
community.gbd_hint: The instance hash in the Global Benchmark Database; we fetch the file from there.
community.family_hint: Lowercase letters, digits and dashes, e.g. scheduling or crypto-sha1.
community.description_hint: Where it comes from and what it encodes.
community.license: I made this formula or may share it, and I license it under CC BY 4.0 so the Dojo can publish it.

metrics.title: Beyond PAR-2
metrics.intro: PAR-2 decides the ranking. These views show what it hides, the way SAT researchers look at results. All of them are also in /dojo/board.json and in the archive's results.json.
metrics.answers: Like the SAT Competition, every score is split by answer: a local search solver can shine on satisfiable formulas and never prove one unsatisfiable. While a season runs, the mystery family stays out of SAT and UNSAT, since its share of satisfiable formulas would reveal it.
metrics.cactus: Each solver's solved formulas sorted by fuel: point k is its k-th fastest formula, so the curve shows how far it gets with how much fuel. A curve says nothing about which formula a point is, so it keeps the hidden set secret, and fuel is rounded to three digits so a solver can't smuggle out what it reads. The virtual best solver (VBS) takes the best result of any ranked solver on every formula: the state of the art of the field.
metrics.marginal: How much worse the VBS gets without a solver: its PAR-2 without the solver minus with it. Share is the measure the Sparkle SAT Challenge 2018 ranked by: log10 of PAR-2 without over PAR-2 with, as a share of all solvers' values. A solver that only duplicates another adds nothing, however fast it is.
metrics.sota: From the theorem proving competition CASC: each formula a solver solves earns it 1 divided by the number of solvers that solve it. CASC averages over the solved formulas; we sum, so solving more never lowers it, and the sums add up to the formulas the VBS solves.
metrics.shapley: Standalone scores reward near-clones, marginal contributions punish them. The Shapley value from cooperative game theory is fair to both: it splits the fuel the whole field saves over solving nothing by each solver's average marginal contribution over every order of joining (Fréchette et al., AAAI 2016). We compute it exactly, in billions of fuel per formula; the values add up to twice the budget minus the VBS's PAR-2.
metrics.budget: The ranking measures a short race: 7 billion fuel per formula, about half a second of a native solver, where the SAT Competition allows 5,000 seconds. Solvers with heavy preprocessing and inprocessing, like Kissat and CaDiCaL, pay for it before it pays off, so at this budget they rank behind MiniSat. Every run goes on to four times the budget, and since fuel is deterministic one run gives the exact score at every smaller budget: the Budget view shows how the ranking changes with more time.
